# Ramonyx — llms-full (public)

> Full public corpus for agents: public machine layer (JSON) + public documentation.
> Source: repo RamonyxJS/ramonyx (https://ramonyx.devmoon.net). Internal docs are never included.

## Search

This site has a search endpoint: https://context7.com/api/v2/ask?siteKey=ask_89339fd8bad939f239a589fa&query=<URL-encoded question>. It returns documentation that answers the question, with a source link for each part. No API key is needed. If nothing matches, it says so.

Context7 library: https://context7.com/websites/ramonyx_devmoon_net

      "scope": "framework",

{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "terms": [
    {
      "term": "SSR (Server-Side Rendering)",
      "definition": "Render React di server menjadi HTML; dua mode: sinkron (`renderToString`) dan streaming (opt-in `streaming: true`, `renderToReadableStream`).",
      "related": [
        "Hydration",
        "Streaming SSR"
      ],

      "related": [
        "SSR (Server-Side Rendering)",
        "Suspense"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/engineering/adr/0047-ssr-streaming.md"
    },
    {
      "term": "Hydration",
      "definition": "Mengaktifkan React di browser atas HTML SSR: payload inline `window.__RAMONYX__` + satu bundle client + `hydrateRoot`. Halaman error tidak di-hydrate.",
      "related": [
        "SSR (Server-Side Rendering)",
        "Soft navigation"
      ],
      "docs": "docs/public/engineering/adr/0007-hydration.md"
    },

      "related": [

      ]
    },

        "Gate report-only"

    },

## docs/public/api/core-contract.md

# API Reference

The public API surface, grouped by package. Everything is ESM, TypeScript-first, and edge-safe
unless noted.

## `ramonyx` (meta package)

Re-exports the common primitives:

```ts
import {
  route, createHandler, HttpError, defineConfig, resolveConfig,
  createCache, createMemoryStore, mergeHooks, formDataToObject,
  createTranslator, negotiateLocale, localePath, parseAcceptLanguage,
} from "ramonyx";
```

## Server — `@ramonyx/server`

```ts
createHandler(options): FetchHandler
```

| Option | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routes` | `RouteEntry[]` | required |
| `middleware` | `Middleware[]` | `[]` |
| `env` | `EnvReader` | `process.env` |
| `logger` | `Logger` | console |
| `strictValidation` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `hooks` | `AppHooks` | — |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | `1_048_576` |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `10_000` |
| `maxConcurrent` | `number` | `100` |
| `envFromRequest` | `(request) => EnvReader?` | — |

Also: `traceId()`, `requestLogging()`, `createMetrics()`, `createMetricsRoute(metrics)`.

## Core — `@ramonyx/core`

```ts
route<Params, Query, Body, Output>({ handler, params?, query?, body?, output? }): RouteDefinition
```

`handler(context)` receives `{ request, params, query, body, env, log, json(), text(), redirect() }`.
Invalid schema input → `400` with `issues`; invalid output → `500`.

Other exports: `HttpError`, `defineConfig`, `resolveConfig`, `mergeHooks`, `formDataToObject`,
`createCache`, `createMemoryStore`, `createTranslator`, `negotiateLocale`, `localePath`,
`parseAcceptLanguage`.

## SSR — `@ramonyx/ssr`

```ts
createPageRoutes({
  pages, renderer, document?, client?, streaming?, hooks?, cache?,
  assets?, i18n?, errorDetails?, maxDocumentBytes?,
}): RouteEntry[]
```

- `client: { script, extraModules? }` enables hydration.
- `i18n: { locales, defaultLocale, prefixDefaultLocale?, directions? }` enables locale routing.
- `document` overrides the HTML shell (`DocumentOptions` includes `title, body, head, scripts,
  status, lang, dir`).

Also: `defaultDocument`, `RAMONYX_MOUNT_ID`, and SEO helpers `sitemapXml`, `robotsTxt`,
`createSeoRoutes`.

## React — `@ramonyx/react`

- `createReactRenderer()` — SSR + streaming renderer.
- `Image` (`@ramonyx/react/assets`) — safe defaults + `<picture>` when variants exist.
- `Link` (`@ramonyx/react/link`) — client navigation + prefetch.
- Types: `PageProps<Data, Params>`, `LayoutProps`, `ErrorPageProps`.

## Compiler — `@ramonyx/compiler`

- `createRouteManifest({ dir, importer? })` — API routes.
- `loadPageRoutes({ dir, apiDir?, importer? })` — page manifest.
- `generateClientEntry(pages, { from })`, `generateServerEntry(options)`,
  `generateRouteTypes(pages)`.
- Loader: `import "@ramonyx/compiler/register"` (TypeScript + JSX for app code).

## Bundler — `@ramonyx/bundler`

- `buildClient(options)`, `buildEdge(options)`, `prerenderRoutes(options)`.
- `readClientScript(clientDir)`, `createAssetResolver(clientDir, { fallbackToPath? })`,
  `assetUrl(manifest, path)`, `readAssetManifest`, `fontPreloadTag`.
- `definePlugin`, `loadPlugins`, `createDevServer`.

## Security — `@ramonyx/security`

`securityHeaders()`, `cspNonce()`, `csrfProtection()`, `rateLimit()`, `parseCookies()`,
`serializeCookie()`, `signValue()`, `verifyValue()`, `createSession()`. The SSRF-guarded fetch is a
Node-only subpath: `import { guardedFetch } from "@ramonyx/security/ssrf"`.

## Adapter runtime — `@ramonyx/adapter-runtime`

`createNodeHost()` (`serve`, `env`), `serveStatic({ dir, prefix, immutable?, headers? })`, and the
in-memory host used by tests. `cacheControl({ maxAge, sMaxAge?, staleWhileRevalidate?, immutable?,
private? })` lives in `@ramonyx/core` (re-exported by `ramonyx`).

## Testing — `@ramonyx/testing`

`createTestServer(options)` / `createTestServerFromHandler(handler)` — in-process requests without
binding a port.

## CLI — `@ramonyx/devtools`

`ramonyx dev | build | start | doctor | version | help`. Build flags: `--static`, `--target edge`,
`--watch`. Dev prints a devtools panel URL (`/__ramonyx/devtools`).

## Diagnostics

Framework errors carry stable `RMX-*` codes. In development, error pages include the stack and
source file; production pages never do.

## docs/public/architecture.md

# Architecture

Ramonyx is a Node.js-first framework with an experimental Rust/V8 runtime. This page describes the
public architecture: how a request flows, what the packages do, and where the boundaries are.

## Request lifecycle

```
Request
  → runtime host (Node adapter)
  → server: body/timeout/concurrency gates
  → global middleware (security headers, CSP nonce, rate limit, logging)
  → router (API routes + page routes, 404/405)
  → folder middleware (root → deepest)
  → loader (GET) / action (POST)
  → render (React: sync or stream)
  → hydration payload + HTML document
Response
```

## Layers

| Layer | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| **Framework** | routing, SSR, server actions, data loading, client navigation, security defaults |
| **Compiler/bundler** | route manifest, codegen (client entry, typed routes, edge entry), Vite builds |
| **Runtime** | Node.js (baseline) or the experimental Rust/V8 host |
| **System** | OS, TCP/TLS, filesystem, process |

## Packages

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `ramonyx` | meta package re-exporting common primitives |
| `@ramonyx/core` | request lifecycle, context, middleware, errors, cache, i18n, assets types |
| `@ramonyx/router` | route matching, params, 404/405 |
| `@ramonyx/server` | HTTP wiring, limits, rate limit, observability |
| `@ramonyx/schema` | Standard Schema validation + error mapping |
| `@ramonyx/adapter-runtime` | runtime contract, Node + in-memory hosts, static serving |
| `@ramonyx/ssr` | page rendering, streaming, SEO helpers, locale routing |
| `@ramonyx/react` | React renderer, `Image`, `Link` |
| `@ramonyx/compiler` | page/API manifests, codegen, dev loader |
| `@ramonyx/bundler` | Vite builds, dev server, assets, plugins |
| `@ramonyx/security` | headers, CSP, CSRF, rate limit, cookies/sessions, SSRF guard |
| `@ramonyx/testing` | in-memory test server |
| `@ramonyx/devtools` | the `ramonyx` CLI |
| `@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server` | MCP server over stdio for agents |
| `@ramonyx/plugin-image` | build-time image variants (optional `sharp`) |

## Server ↔ client boundary

- Page/layout modules are isomorphic; loaders and actions are server-only.
- `*.server.ts` modules are stubbed with a poison pill in the client bundle.
- The build rejects `node:*` imports in client modules and scans the output for leaks.
- Secrets belong in `*.server.ts` or server-only loaders; only UI data goes into the hydration
  payload (JSON-serializable).

## Runtime contract

`@ramonyx/core` defines the web-standard boundary used by every host:

```ts
export type FetchHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;

export interface RuntimeHost {
  readonly name: string;                    // "node" | "memory" | "ramonyx"
  serve(handler: FetchHandler, options: { port: number; host?: string }): Promise<RunningServer>;
  readonly env: { get(name: string): string | undefined };
}
```

The Node adapter and the in-memory test host implement it; the experimental Rust/V8 runtime targets
the same contract (compatibility suite). The framework does not depend on runtime internals.

## Rendering & deployment targets

- **Node**: SSR + hydration + soft navigation; streaming opt-in.
- **Static**: prerendered pages + assets (`ramonyx build --static`).
- **Edge**: a single `{ fetch }` artifact with statically imported routes and an inlined asset map
  (CI exercises it in workerd).

See [Routing](routing.md), [SSR & Hydration](ssr-hydration.md), and [Deployment](deployment.md).

## docs/public/assets-and-images.md

# Assets & Images

Files in `src/assets/**` are hashed at build time, recorded in a manifest, and resolved through the
server-side asset resolver. Node cannot `import photo.png`, so the resolver is the contract between
SSR and the client bundle.

## Add an asset

```
src/assets/
  logo.svg
  img/hero.png
  fonts/inter.woff2
```

Wire the resolver once in `src/app.ts`:

```ts
import { createAssetResolver } from "@ramonyx/bundler";

const assets = await createAssetResolver(clientDir, { fallbackToPath: true });

createPageRoutes({ pages, renderer, assets /* ... */ });
```

Loaders receive `assets`:

```ts
export async function loader({ assets }) {
  return {
    logo: assets.url("logo.svg"),        // "/assets/logo-3f9a1c2b7d.svg"
    hero: assets.image("img/hero.png"),  // { src, width, height, srcSet?, sources? }
  };
}
```

## Rendering images

`Image` from `@ramonyx/react/assets` supplies safe defaults: explicit dimensions (no layout shift),
`loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, and an optional `<picture>` when responsive variants exist.

```tsx
import { Image } from "@ramonyx/react/assets";

<Image {...data.hero} alt="Hero" sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 640px" />;
```

With the image plugin enabled, `assets.image()` returns `srcSet` and `<source>` entries, so the
markup renders:

```html
<picture>
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="/assets/img/hero-320-….webp 320w, …" sizes="…" />
  <img src="/assets/img/hero-….png" width="800" height="600" srcset="…" … />
</picture>
```

## Responsive images (build-time variants)

```bash
pnpm add @ramonyx/plugin-image sharp
```

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
import { imageOptimizer } from "@ramonyx/plugin-image";
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [imageOptimizer({ widths: [320, 640, 960, 1280], formats: ["webp"] })],
});
```

- Variants are generated at build time (resize + WebP; AVIF is opt-in because it is slower).
- `sharp` is an **optional peer** — installed by the app, not by the framework.
- Results are cached by content hash in `.ramonyx/image-cache`; unchanged images are not re-encoded.
- The original file is always copied and used as the universal fallback.
- Colors/dimensions are recorded in `ramonyx.assets.json` (`width`, `height`, `variants`).

`avif` can be added to `formats` for smaller files at the cost of build time. SVG is passed through
(vector assets do not need variants).

## Fonts

Fonts are hashed like any asset. Preload a font by putting a `<link rel="preload">` tag in page
metadata:

```ts
import { fontPreloadTag } from "@ramonyx/bundler";

export const metadata = {
  title: "Home",
  head: fontPreloadTag("/assets/fonts/inter-6a1b2c3d.woff2"),
};
```

## Honest limitations

- Development serves `src/assets/**` as-is (no hashes, no variants); build output is the source of
  truth for production behavior.
- No blur placeholders (LQIP) or on-demand dev variants yet.
- Image optimization only runs for raster formats (PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF/TIFF).

## docs/public/benchmarks.md

# Benchmarks

Performance claims need measurements you can run. The benchmark protocol is fixed: warm up, repeat,
report the distribution (median, spread) — never a single run, never an average hiding a tail.

## What is measured

| Benchmark | Metric | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP | requests/s, p50/p95/p99 | autocannon against the playground |
| SSR | render time, TTFB, output size | synchronous vs streaming, in-process |
| Security | status/error counts, RSS under abuse/soak | 6 abuse scenarios + sustained load |
| Startup | wall/startup/load/eval | Rust runtime CLI, median of N runs |
| Web Vitals | LCP, CLS, FCP, TTFB | Playwright on the production build |
| Image pipeline | before/after LCP/CLS with variants | throttled CDP + cold loads |

## Commands

```bash
pnpm bench                 # HTTP baseline (warm-up 3s + 5 runs, median/spread)
pnpm bench:report          # compare against baseline (report-only, tolerance 25%)
pnpm bench:ssr             # SSR sync vs streaming
pnpm bench:ssr:report      # comparison artifact
pnpm bench:security        # abuse cases + soak (RSS from /proc)
pnpm bench:image           # image pipeline before/after (playground)
benchmarks/runtime-startup.sh   # Rust runtime startup (needs a release build)
```

Results are written under `benchmarks/results/`. Web Vitals are measured by the e2e suite and
compared report-only against the committed baseline.

## Baselines are per environment

A baseline is only meaningful on the machine that produced it. Baselines are stored per
(platform × arch × Node major × CPU), and the strict comparison **refuses to compare across
environments** — it prints the mismatching fields instead of pretending.

- Development baselines are committed for the maintainer machine.
- CI runs benchmarks **report-only**: GitHub-hosted runners vary too much for a blocking gate.
- `VITALS_STRICT=1` turns the Web Vitals comparison into a gate; use it only on a stable runner.

## Rules

- Same hardware/OS/runtime/config for every comparison.
- Identical work per request; verify responses match.
- Report medians and spread; keep raw artifacts.
- No public performance claim without a runnable benchmark in the repo.

## docs/public/cli.md

# CLI Reference

The `ramonyx` CLI (from `@ramonyx/devtools`) runs the app: dev server, build, production start, and
diagnostics.

```bash
ramonyx dev              # Vite + HMR (default :5173) → SSR (port from config)
ramonyx build            # client bundle → dist/client (run before production start)
ramonyx build --static   # client bundle + prerender pages → dist/static
ramonyx build --target edge   # server/edge bundle → dist/edge ({ fetch } contract)
ramonyx build --watch    # rebuild on file changes (covers --static/--target)
ramonyx start            # production SSR (NODE_ENV=production)
ramonyx doctor           # config + routes + build diagnostics
ramonyx version | help
```

## Flags

| Flag | Applies to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app <dir>` | all | App directory (default: cwd) |
| `--config <path>` | all | Config path (default `<app>/ramonyx.config.ts`) |
| `--port <n>` | dev/start | Override the SSR port |
| `--dev-port <n>` | dev | Override the Vite port (default 5173) |
| `--static` | build | Prerender static routes (`getStaticPaths` for dynamic routes) → `dist/static` |
| `--target <name>` | build | Extra target; `edge` → `dist/edge` |
| `--watch` | build | Rebuild on changes (debounced, safe queue) |

## Conventions

```
src/app.ts             export createApp(options?) → FetchHandler
src/server.ts          optional custom server entry (CLI still hosts it)
src/routes/            page.tsx / layout.tsx / error.tsx + api/*.ts
ramonyx.config.ts      default export { app?, server? } (optional)
```

- `ramonyx dev|start` prefers `src/server.ts` when present, otherwise `src/app.ts`.
- Plugins from `ramonyx.config.ts` are loaded by the CLI (Vite, middleware, hooks, assets).
- `ramonyx start` sets `NODE_ENV=production` if unset; reactivity/React production build depends on it.
- `--static` and `--target edge` cannot be combined (different artifacts).

## Examples

```bash
# Local development with HMR
ramonyx dev --app examples/shop

# Production build + start on port 8080
ramonyx build --app examples/shop
ramonyx start --app examples/shop --port 8080

# Static export and edge artifact
ramonyx build --static --app examples/shop
ramonyx build --target edge --app examples/shop
ramonyx build --watch --app examples/shop
```

## Doctor

`ramonyx doctor` prints the CLI/Node versions, resolved config, whether `src/app.ts` exists, the
number of pages, and whether `dist/client` has a manifest. Use it before filing an issue.

## Devtools

`ramonyx dev` also prints the devtools panel URL (`/__ramonyx/devtools`). See
[Devtools Panel](devtools.md).

## docs/public/data-and-caching.md

# Data & Caching

Ramonyx keeps data loading in the page module: a `loader` for reads, an `action` for writes, and an
opt-in cache for expensive work.

## Loaders

```ts
export const revalidate = 60;
export const cacheTags = ["catalog"];

export async function loader({ params }) {
  return { product: await db.products.find(params.id) };
}
```

Loader data is JSON-serializable and available to the component as `data` (and to the client via
the hydration payload).

## Cache semantics

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `revalidate: 60` | Cache loader data for 60 s; the next 60 s serves stale data and refreshes in the background |
| `cacheTags: ["catalog"]` | Tag the entry so `revalidate({ tags: ["catalog"] })` removes it |
| no `revalidate` | No caching — loader runs on every request |

Session safety: requests with **cookies** or a **query string** bypass the cache. That keeps
per-user responses out of a shared cache by construction.

The default cache is in-memory (single process). The store interface (`KeyValueStore`) is pluggable
— implement `get/set/delete/invalidateTags` for Redis or another backend and pass it to
`createCache({ store })`. The contract has a shared test suite in the repo.

## On-demand invalidation

```ts
// from an action
await revalidate({ tags: ["catalog"] });
```

```ts
// from anywhere with the cache instance
import { createCache } from "ramonyx";
const cache = createCache();
await cache.revalidate({ paths: ["/products"], tags: ["catalog"] });
```

Invalidation also fires the `onInvalidate` app hook, so observability and plugins can react.

## Server actions

Actions are POST handlers colocated with the page:

```ts
export const actionSchema = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1,
    vendor: "app",
    validate: (form) => {
      const name = String((form as Record<string, unknown>)?.name ?? "").trim();
      return name.length > 0
        ? { value: { name } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "Name is required", path: ["name"] }] };
    },
  },
};

export async function action({ formData, revalidate }) {
  const name = String(formData.get("name"));
  await db.customers.create({ name });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["customers"] });
  return { message: `Created ${name}` };
}
```

`actionSchema` validates the form data before the action runs (invalid → `400` + field errors). The
page renders the last action result as `action` (`{ ok, errors?, message?, data? }`). Redirects use
`303` so a refresh does not resubmit.

## Pragmatic notes

- The cache key includes the page path, route params, and (with i18n) the active locale.
- Cached values are process-local; for multi-instance deployments use an external store.
- There is no HTML page cache (CSP nonces make HTML per-request); only **loader data** is cached.
- A CDN can cache the HTML of static/prerendered pages separately.

## docs/public/deployment.md

# Deployment

One app, three targets. The same `src/app.ts` runs on Node, as static files, or as an edge
`fetch` handler.

## Node (default)

```bash
ramonyx build        # client bundle → dist/client (hashed assets + manifest)
ramonyx start        # SSR on the configured port; NODE_ENV=production
```

Set the port/host in `ramonyx.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";
export default defineConfig({ server: { port: 3000, host: "0.0.0.0" } });
```

Production notes:

- Serve `dist/client/assets/**` with `immutable` cache headers (the CLI's `start` does this for you).
- The Node adapter compresses responses with brotli/gzip and appends per-chunk for streaming.
- Keep the process behind a reverse proxy for TLS; the runtime verifies TLS for outbound `fetch`.
- Defaults: body 1 MiB, timeout 10 s, concurrency 100. Tune via `createHandler` options.

## Static

```bash
ramonyx build --static     # → dist/static
```

- Static routes are prerendered; dynamic routes need `getStaticPaths`.
- A page with `metadata.status = 404` becomes `404.html`.
- Assets are copied alongside the HTML.
- Deploy the directory to any static host (GitHub Pages, S3, Netlify, …).

## Edge / serverless

```bash
ramonyx build --target edge   # → dist/edge/index.js
```

The artifact exports `{ fetch }` — the standard edge contract:

```js
export const fetch = (request, env) => handler(request);
export default { fetch };
```

- Pages, API routes, actions, middleware, and the asset map are inlined into one bundle.
- Platform bindings (KV, secrets) are forwarded per request: the entry receives `env` and exposes
  it to loaders/actions as `env.get(name)` / `env.getRaw(name)`.
- The build rejects `node:*` imports in the edge artifact (except where shimmed by the platform).
- CI runs a **workerd** smoke test against the edge artifact (Cloudflare's runtime), so SSR, API,
  actions, env bindings, middleware, and 404s are exercised in a real edge runtime.

## Preview and staging

- Local preview: `pnpm docs` (and `pnpm dev` for the playground).
- Worker preview: run `pnpm build:worker` then `pnpm dlx wrangler deploy`, or trigger
  `deploy-worker.yml` manually. The canonical domain is `https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/`; the
  GitHub Pages mirror is published at `/ramonyx`.
- **Automatic PR previews are intentionally not enabled.** Cloudflare credentials are limited to
  trusted `main`/manual workflows so pull requests (especially forks) never receive deployment
  secrets. A PR is previewed locally or via an explicitly authorized manual deploy.

## Environment variables

| Context | Access |
| --- | --- |
| Node | `env.get("NAME")` (process env by default) |
| Edge | per-request `env` bindings forwarded by the platform adapter |
| Client | never — server values stay server-side |

## Headers & security in production

- `securityHeaders()` + `cspNonce()` from `@ramonyx/security` set CSP (with per-request nonce),
  `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`.
- HSTS/TLS termination belongs to your proxy or platform.
- Rate limiting and load shedding are in-process by default; use an external store for
  multi-instance deployments.

## docs/public/devtools.md

# Devtools Panel

Every `ramonyx dev` session exposes a dev-only panel with routes, request/loader/render timings,
hydration status, and bundle sizes. It is never enabled in production builds.

```bash
ramonyx dev
# dev: http://localhost:5173 (Vite + HMR) → SSR http://127.0.0.1:3000
# devtools: http://localhost:5173/__ramonyx/devtools
```

## What it shows

| Section | Data source | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Routes** | Page manifest | Updated when route files change (same watcher as client entry regeneration) |
| **Bundles & assets** | `dist/client/ramonyx.assets.json` + file sizes | Empty until the app has been built — the panel does not build for you |
| **Recent requests** | Collector middleware + `AppHooks` | Last 50 requests; method, path, status, total, loader, render, cache, hydration |

**Hydration** is detected from the response HTML: `payload` when
`<script id="ramonyx-payload">` is present, `none` for HTML without it (e.g. error pages).

## How it works

- The dev server creates a collector backed by the app's `AppHooks` (`onLoaderEnd`, `onRenderEnd`)
  and a middleware placed outermost in the chain.
- `GET /__ramonyx/devtools` serves the panel (a self-contained HTML page polling every 2s);
  `GET /__ramonyx/data` returns `{ routes, assets, requests }` as JSON.
- Both endpoints are served by the dev server, not proxied to the SSR app, and are absent from
  production.

## Limitations (honest)

- Loader/render events do not carry a request id; the panel correlates them to the **last open
  request with the same path**. Good enough for low-concurrency development.
- Page routes only (API routes are not listed separately).
- Requests short-circuited by plugin middleware are still recorded (the collector is outermost), but
  Vite asset requests and `/__ramonyx/*` calls are not.
- Not a production observability tool — use [Observability](observability.md) for that.

## docs/public/for-agents.md

# For Agents

Agents get a machine-readable view of Ramonyx that is generated from **public** documentation only:

- [`llms.txt`](https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/machine/llms.txt) — index of the public docs and
  machine files.
- [`llms-full.txt`](https://ramonyx.devmoon.net/machine/llms-full.txt) — the same content in
  one file.
- `machine/features.json` — feature status, packages, evidence, and honest limitations.
- `machine/rules.json` — rules for writing apps with good/bad examples.
- `machine/adrs.json` — public decision summaries (one-line decisions + relations).
- `machine/stats.json` — the single source of truth for numbers (version, packages, tests).
- `machine/api.json`, `machine/cli.json`, `machine/config.schema.json` — extracted API/CLI/config
  references.

## Context7

- Library listing: [ramonyx_devmoon_net](https://context7.com/websites/ramonyx_devmoon_net)
- Search endpoint: `https://context7.com/api/v2/ask?siteKey=ask_89339fd8bad939f239a589fa&query=<URL-encoded question>`
  — returns documentation with source links; no API key required.

## MCP server (stdio)

The docs are also available as an MCP server with five tools — `search_docs`, `get_page`,
`get_feature_status`, `get_rules`, `list_adrs`:

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add ramonyx-docs -- npx -y @ramonyx/mcp-docs-server
```

```json
// Cursor: .cursor/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ramonyx-docs": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server"] }
  }
}
```

```json
// OpenCode: opencode.json
{
  "mcp": {
    "ramonyx-docs": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@ramonyx/mcp-docs-server"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

The server ships a **snapshot of the public docs** at release time, so it works without cloning the
repo. Inside the repository you can point it at the working tree:

```bash
node --import ./tools/register.mjs packages/mcp-docs-server/src/cli.ts --docs docs/public
```

## Ground rules for agents

1. **Facts over guesses.** Feature status comes from `features.json`; numbers from `stats.json`.
2. **Check the limitations field.** Features marked `partial`/`experimental` have documented gaps.
3. **Prefer the public contract.** If something is not in the public docs, do not assume it exists.
4. **Every claim needs evidence.** The machine layer links code/test/ADR paths; follow them.

## docs/public/getting-started.md

# Getting Started

Build a full-stack TypeScript app with file routing, SSR React, and secure defaults. Ramonyx runs
on **Node.js ≥ 24**; the Rust/V8 runtime is experimental.

```bash
pnpm create ramonyx-app my-app
cd my-app
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # Vite (5173) → SSR (3000)
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. The scaffold ships with a page, an API route, validation, actions,
security middleware, and hydration — all runnable.

## Project layout

```
src/app.ts             createApp() → fetch handler (API + pages + middleware)
src/server.ts          optional custom server entry (CLI still hosts it)
src/routes/            file routing
  page.tsx             route "/"
  layout.tsx           root layout
  [...slug]/page.tsx   404 page (metadata.status = 404)
  middleware.ts        per-folder middleware (root = every route)
  api/halo/[nama].ts   dynamic API route
ramonyx.config.ts      app/server options (optional)
```

## A page with a loader

`src/routes/page.tsx` is an isomorphic module: `loader` runs on the server, the component renders
on the server and then hydrates in the browser.

```tsx
import type { PageProps } from "@ramonyx/react";

export const metadata = { title: "Home", description: "My first app" };

export async function loader() {
  return { message: "Hello from the server" };
}

export default function Home({ data }: PageProps<{ message: string }>) {
  return <h1>{data.message}</h1>;
}
```

Loader data must be JSON-serializable (it is embedded in the hydration payload). For
filesystem/database access, use a `*.server.ts` module — the client bundle gets a poison-pill stub
instead of your secrets.

## An API route with validation

`src/routes/api/halo/[nama].ts`:

```ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";
import type { StandardSchema } from "@ramonyx/schema";

const params: StandardSchema<unknown, { nama: string }> = {
  "~standard": {
    version: 1,
    vendor: "my-app",
    validate: (value) =>
      typeof (value as Record<string, unknown>)?.nama === "string"
        ? { value: { nama: (value as { nama: string }).nama } }
        : { issues: [{ message: "nama wajib", path: ["nama"] }] },
  },
};

export const GET = route<{ nama: string }>({
  params,
  handler: ({ params, json }) => json({ hello: params.nama }),
});
```

Invalid input returns `400` with `issues` before your handler runs.

## A form action

```tsx
export async function action({ formData }: { formData: FormData }) {
  const name = String(formData.get("name") ?? "").trim();
  if (name.length === 0) return { errors: { name: "Required" } };
  return { message: `Hello, ${name}!` };
}
```

The runtime re-renders the page with the action result, and the browser intercepts submission so
it works without a page reload — while still working with JavaScript disabled (progressive
enhancement, `POST` + `303` PRG).

## Build & deploy

```bash
ramonyx build             # client bundle → dist/client
ramonyx start             # production SSR (NODE_ENV=production)
ramonyx build --static    # prerender → dist/static (host anywhere)
ramonyx build --target edge   # dist/edge/index.js ({ fetch } contract)
```

See [Deployment](deployment.md) for details, and [Routing](routing.md) /
[SSR & Hydration](ssr-hydration.md) for the runtime model.

## docs/public/i18n.md

# Internationalization

Locale routing and translation helpers are built in — no module, no dependency. Enable routing,
translate in loaders/components, and let the framework handle `<html lang>`, `hreflang`, and
per-locale caching.

## Enable locale routing

```ts
// src/app.ts
createPageRoutes({
  pages,
  renderer: createReactRenderer(),
  i18n: {
    locales: ["en", "id"],
    defaultLocale: "en",
    // prefixDefaultLocale: true,     // every locale gets a prefix (incl. default)
    // directions: { ar: "rtl" },     // <html dir="rtl"> for specific locales
  },
});
```

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/about` | Served as the **default** locale (no prefix) |
| `/id/about` | Served as `id` |
| `/en` · `/en/about` | **308** → `/` · `/about` (when the default locale is unprefixed) |
| `prefixDefaultLocale: true` | The inverse: `/about` → 308 `/en/about` |

The framework also:

- sets `<html lang="…">` (and `dir` when configured);
- emits `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="…">` for every locale plus `x-default`;
- passes `locale` to loaders, actions, page props (`PageProps.locale`), and the hydration payload;
- **includes the locale in loader cache keys**, so revalidated pages cannot leak data across
  languages;
- leaves API routes untouched.

## Translating

Catalogs are plain nested objects (JSON-friendly). Load them where the data lives and pass them to
`createTranslator`:

```tsx
import { createTranslator, type Messages } from "ramonyx";

const catalog: Record<string, Messages> = {
  en: { hello: "Hello {name}!", items: { one: "{count} item", other: "{count} items" } },
  id: { hello: "Halo {name}!", items: { one: "{count} item", other: "{count} item" } },
};

export async function loader({ locale }: { locale?: string }) {
  const active = locale ?? "en";
  const { t, formatNumber, formatDate } = createTranslator({
    locale: active,
    messages: catalog[active] ?? {},
    fallbackMessages: catalog.en,        // optional
    // onMissing: (key) => console.warn("i18n:", key),
  });
  return {
    greeting: t("hello", { name: "Rina" }),
    count: t("items", { count: 3 }),      // plural via Intl.PluralRules
    price: formatNumber(1234.5),
    date: formatDate(new Date(), { dateStyle: "long" }),
  };
}
```

- **Interpolation**: `{name}` is replaced from the params object; unknown params stay as written.
- **Plural**: object values (`one`/`other`/…) are selected with `Intl.PluralRules` using
  `params.count`.
- **Fallback**: missing key → `fallbackMessages` → `onMissing(key)` → the key itself.
- The helper is pure and edge-safe; it can also be used in middleware or client components.

## Language switcher

```tsx
import { localePath } from "ramonyx";

// From any page, build the same page in another locale (existing prefix is stripped).
<a href={localePath(currentPath, "id", { locales: ["en", "id"], defaultLocale: "en" })}>
  Bahasa Indonesia
</a>
```

## `Accept-Language` negotiation (middleware)

The framework does **not** auto-detect or auto-redirect: explicit behavior is cache- and SEO-friendly.
Use the helper in pre-routing middleware with a cookie:

```ts
import { negotiateLocale, localePath } from "ramonyx";
import { parseCookies, serializeCookie } from "@ramonyx/security";

const i18n = { locales: ["en", "id"], defaultLocale: "en" } as const;

export async function localeMiddleware(context, next) {
  const url = new URL(context.request.url);
  if (url.pathname !== "/") return next();
  const saved = parseCookies(context.request.headers.get("cookie") ?? "").locale;
  const locale = saved ?? negotiateLocale(context.request.headers.get("accept-language"), i18n);
  return new Response(null, {
    status: 302,
    headers: {
      location: localePath("/", locale, i18n),
      "set-cookie": serializeCookie("locale", locale, { path: "/", httpOnly: false, sameSite: "lax" }),
    },
  });
}
```

## Limitations (honest)

- No ICU MessageFormat (interpolation + `Intl` plural categories only).
- No automatic detection/redirect; use the middleware pattern above.
- Catalogs are app-provided (JSON/data store) — the framework does not load files for you.
- One route per locale (linear in the number of locales); per-route localization is not supported.
- `hreflang` uses the page's logical path; dynamic routes follow the currently requested params.

## docs/public/observability.md

# Observability

Three edge-safe primitives, built on the existing middleware + hook system (no dependency):

1. **Trace id** per request (`traceId()`) — propagated or generated, readable in loaders/actions.
2. **Structured request logs** (`requestLogging()`) — method, path, status, duration, trace id.
3. **Metrics** (`createMetrics()`) — counters/latencies from app hooks, exposed as JSON.

## Wiring

```ts
// src/app.ts
import { createMetrics, createMetricsRoute, requestLogging, traceId } from "@ramonyx/server";
import { mergeHooks } from "ramonyx";

const metrics = createMetrics();

const handler = createHandler({
  routes: [
    ...apiRoutes,
    createMetricsRoute(metrics),   // GET /metrics
    ...createPageRoutes({ pages, renderer, hooks: mergeHooks(appHooks, metrics.hooks) }),
  ],
  middleware: [traceId(), requestLogging()],
  hooks: mergeHooks(appHooks, metrics.hooks),
});
```

Order matters: `traceId()` must run before `requestLogging()` so the log line carries the id.

## Trace id

- Uses the incoming `x-request-id` header when present (proxy/client propagation), otherwise
  generates one (UUID, with a `getRandomValues` fallback).
- Rewrites the request with the header set, so loaders/actions can read it; sets the same header on
  the response.

```ts
// inside a loader
const id = request.headers.get("x-request-id");
```

Custom header name: `traceId({ header: "x-trace-id" })`.

## Structured logs

```ts
requestLogging();                    // message "request"
requestLogging({ message: "http" }); // custom message
```

`requestLogging()` emits one `info` line per request through the app logger:

```json
{"level":"info","message":"request","method":"GET","path":"/","status":200,"ms":12,"traceId":"…"}
```

Ship it to any collector (Fluent Bit, Vector, OTLP log exporter). Secrets/PII must not be logged —
the framework only emits method/path/status/duration/trace id.

## Metrics

`createMetrics()` returns `{ hooks, snapshot() }`:

```json
{
  "requests": { "total": 120, "byStatusClass": { "2xx": 118, "5xx": 2 },
                "durationMs": { "sum": 1840, "count": 120, "max": 210 } },
  "loaders": { "count": 80, "cached": 42, "durationMs": { "sum": 620, "max": 90 } },
  "renders": { "count": 118, "streaming": 110, "durationMs": { "sum": 980, "max": 140 } },
  "invalidations": 3
}
```

- `createMetricsRoute(metrics, { path: "/metrics" })` serves the snapshot as JSON.
- Schedule `metrics.snapshot()` exports to OTLP/Prometheus from your platform, or pull `/metrics`.
- Counters are cumulative since process start (per instance).

## Notes & limitations

- `traceId` is a correlation id, not a full W3C `traceparent`; native OpenTelemetry spans are not
  built in (candidate if there is demand).
- Metrics are process-local: multi-instance deployments should scrape each instance or aggregate in
  your platform.
- The hooks are zero-cost when unused; the helpers are edge-safe (no `node:*`).

## docs/public/plugins.md

# Plugins

A plugin extends an app at build time (Vite), at request time (middleware), through app hooks
(observability/caching), and through the asset pipeline.

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
import { imageOptimizer } from "@ramonyx/plugin-image";
import { defineConfig } from "ramonyx";
import { analytics } from "./src/plugins/analytics.ts";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [analytics(), imageOptimizer()],
});
```

`ramonyx dev|build|start` loads plugins from the config. A custom server entry (`src/server.ts`)
still receives their hooks and is wrapped by their middleware — plugins are never duplicated.

## Writing a plugin

```ts
// src/plugins/analytics.ts
import { definePlugin } from "@ramonyx/bundler";
import type { Middleware } from "ramonyx";

const middleware: Middleware = async (context, next) => {
  const started = performance.now();
  const response = await next();
  console.log(context.request.method, new URL(context.request.url).pathname, response.status, Math.round(performance.now() - started));
  return response;
};

export const analytics = () =>
  definePlugin({
    name: "analytics",
    middleware: () => middleware,
    hooks: () => ({
      onLoaderEnd: (event) => {
        /* record loader timing */
      },
    }),
  });
```

| Hook | Runs | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vite` | build/dev | extra Vite plugins (CSS, fonts, aliases) |
| `middleware` | before routing | logging, headers, early blocking |
| `hooks` | request lifecycle | timing, metrics, invalidation |
| `assets` | build, per file | derived outputs (image variants) + dimensions |

`middleware` must be edge-safe (no `node:*`) if you deploy the edge artifact. Middleware runs
**before** application middleware, in plugin order.

## Asset hook

```ts
export const plugin = definePlugin({
  name: "thumbnails",
  async assets(_context, asset) {
    if (!asset.path.endsWith(".png")) return undefined;
    return {
      meta: { width: 800, height: 600 },
      outputs: [{ path: "img/hero-400.webp", data: encoded, width: 400, format: "webp" }],
    };
  },
});
```

Derived files are hashed automatically and recorded as `variants` in the manifest, so
`assets.image()` and `Image` can render them.

## Publishing a plugin

Third-party plugins live in `node_modules`, where Node does **not** strip TypeScript. Ship compiled
JavaScript:

```json
{
  "name": "ramonyx-plugin-analytics",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "default": "./dist/index.js" } },
  "peerDependencies": { "@ramonyx/bundler": "^0.4.0", "ramonyx": "^0.4.0" },
  "engines": { "node": ">=24" }
}
```

- Use `peerDependencies` (not `dependencies`) so types/contracts follow the app's Ramonyx version.
- Heavy dependencies should be **optional peers** (`peerDependenciesMeta`) and imported lazily with
  a clear error — see how `@ramonyx/plugin-image` treats `sharp`.
- Test the hooks directly and in a real app (`ramonyx build|dev|start`).
- Contract stability: the plugin contract is **stable since 0.4.2**. Breaking changes follow
  semver (minor/major) with migration notes; additive optional hooks remain possible.

## Limitations (honest)

- No plugin registry or `ramonyx add` — install with your package manager.
- No per-route/per-loader plugin hooks (pre-routing middleware + app hooks only).
- Plugin order is config order; there is no explicit priority field.

## docs/public/routing.md

# Routing

Ramonyx maps files under `src/routes/` to URLs. No route config file, no decorators.

```
src/routes/
  page.tsx                 /
  layout.tsx               root layout (wraps every page)
  error.tsx                error boundary for this folder
  [...slug]/page.tsx       catch-all (404 in the template)
  users/
    page.tsx               /users
    [id]/page.tsx          /users/:id
  (marketing)/about/page.tsx   /about        ← route group: parentheses are not in the URL
  api/
    hello.ts               /api/hello
    users/[id].ts          /api/users/:id
```

## Pages

A page module exports:

| Export | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | React component receiving `PageProps` |
| `loader` | server-only data loading (GET) |
| `action` | form mutation handler (POST to the same path) |
| `metadata` | title/description/status/robots/canonical/head |
| `revalidate` | cache TTL in seconds (ISR-lite) |
| `cacheTags` | tags for on-demand invalidation |
| `prerender` / `getStaticPaths` | static generation control |

Dynamic segments use `[param]`; catch-all segments use `[...param]`. Route groups `(name)` organize
files without changing URLs. A folder-level `layout.tsx` wraps pages below it; `error.tsx` renders
when a loader/action/render throws an `HttpError` (or any error), with the status preserved.

## Loaders

```ts
export async function loader({ params, query, request, env, log }) {
  const user = await db.user.find(params.id);
  if (user === null) throw new HttpError(404, "User not found");
  return { user };
}
```

The loader context also exposes `assets` (asset resolver) and `locale` (when i18n routing is
enabled). Loader data is embedded in the hydration payload — keep it JSON-serializable.

## API routes

```ts
// src/routes/api/hello/[nama].ts
import { route } from "ramonyx";

export const GET = route<{ nama: string }>({
  handler: ({ params, json }) => json({ hello: params.nama }),
});

export const POST = route({
  handler: async ({ request }) => Response.json({ received: await request.text() }),
});
```

Exported `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` become allowed methods; others return `405` with an
`Allow` header. Query/params/body can be validated with a Standard Schema; invalid input → `400`
with `issues`.

## Middleware

- `src/routes/middleware.ts` runs before every route in that folder (root = every route), in
  root → deepest order. It is edge-safe: no `node:*` imports.
- Application-wide middleware (static files, logging, security headers) is passed to
  `createHandler({ middleware })` in `src/app.ts`.

```ts
export default [
  securityHeaders(),
  cspNonce(),
  rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowSeconds: 60 }),
];
```

## HTTP limits (secure by default)

| Limit | Default | On exceed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request body | 1 MiB | `413` |
| Handler/loader/render | 10 s | `503` + `request.signal` aborted |
| Concurrent requests | 100 | `503` + `Retry-After` |

Override per app via `createHandler({ maxBodyBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrent })`.

## Typed routes

`ramonyx build` and `ramonyx dev` generate `.ramonyx/routes.ts` with a typed `routeHref()` helper
and a `RouteParamsMap`, so wrong paths or params fail at type-check time. Import it by relative
path from your app code.

## i18n routing

`createPageRoutes({ i18n: { locales: ["en", "id"], defaultLocale: "en" } })` registers a route per
locale (`/id/...`), keeps the default locale unprefixed, sets `<html lang>` + `hreflang`, and
passes `locale` to loaders and page props. See the i18n section in the source docs for the full
guide (translation helper, negotiation, language switcher).

## docs/public/security/overview.md

# Security Overview

Ramonyx is designed to be **secure by default**: limits apply before your code runs, and security
primitives ship in the framework instead of being copy-pasted between apps.

> This page describes mitigations, not guarantees. Security claims without executable tests are not
> made (see the repository's evidence policy). Report vulnerabilities privately via
> [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/RamonyxJS/ramonyx/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

## Defaults that apply to every app

| Control | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Request body limit | 1 MiB → `413` (checked before routing, including streamed bodies) |
| Handler/loader/render timeout | 10 s → `503`, with `request.signal` aborted |
| Concurrent requests | 100 → `503` + `Retry-After` (load shedding) |
| SSR document size | 2 MiB → `500` |
| Client bundle boundary | `node:*` imports and `*.server.ts` modules are rejected/stubbed at build time |

All limits are configurable per app (`createHandler({ maxBodyBytes, timeoutMs, maxConcurrent })`).

## Security primitives

```ts
import {
  cspNonce,
  csrfProtection,
  rateLimit,
  securityHeaders,
} from "@ramonyx/security";

export default [
  securityHeaders(),        // CSP (with nonce), nosniff, referrer policy, frame-ancestors
  cspNonce(),               // per-request nonce injected into the hydration payload
  csrfProtection(),         // double-submit cookie (Web Crypto HMAC, constant-time compare)
  rateLimit({ limit: 120, windowSeconds: 60 }),  // per client; identity from the adapter
];
```

- **CSP nonce** — the nonce travels with the hydration payload, so inline scripts carry the same
  nonce the policy allows. No `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts.
- **CSRF** — double-submit cookie + header, signed with Web Crypto; compare in constant time.
  `trustProxy` is opt-in, so a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` cannot evade rate limits by default.
- **Sessions** — cookie parsing/serialization with safe defaults (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure),
  HMAC-signed values, and a small session helper (`read/commit/clear`).
- **Outbound fetch** — `guardedFetch` (from `@ramonyx/security/ssrf`) rejects private/loopback/
  link-local targets, validates every redirect hop, and **pins the resolved IP** so DNS rebinding
  cannot redirect a connection to an internal address.
- **Input validation** — Standard Schema at the trust boundary (params, query, body, form); invalid
  input returns `400` with field-level `issues` before your handler runs.
- **Output safety** — React escaping everywhere; raw HTML requires an explicit
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; server errors never leak stack traces in production.

## Server/client boundary

Server-only code belongs in `*.server.ts` modules. The build:

1. rejects `node:*` imports in page/layout modules (with a message pointing at the file),
2. replaces `*.server.ts` imports in the **client** bundle with a poison-pill stub,
3. scans the client output for leaked Node built-ins.

A secret placed in a plain shared module can still reach the client — keep secrets in
`*.server.ts` or server-only loaders and pass only what the UI needs.

## Runtime (experimental)

The Rust/V8 runtime is experimental. Its permission model is **deny-all by default**
(`--allow-read|write|net|env` opt-in), with worker/process isolation, resource quotas, and an
OS-level sandbox (Landlock) for plugins. It is not part of the production promise yet.

## Dependency & supply chain

- Lockfile committed; `pnpm audit --audit-level high` in CI and weekly.
- New versions must be at least **24 hours old** before adoption (`minimumReleaseAge`), reducing
  exposure to compromised fresh releases.
- npm releases are published from **verified tarballs** with **provenance** (build → verify →
  publish), guarded by tag↔version checks.

## Limitations (honest)

- Rate limiting and load shedding are process-local; multi-instance deployments need a shared
  store.
- CSP is wired through `@ramonyx/security`; if you replace it, you own the policy.
- CSRF protection covers double-submit verification; hidden-field verification for non-JS form
  flows is not implemented.
- The experimental runtime has not had an external security audit.

## docs/public/sessions-and-auth.md

# Sessions & Auth Primitives

Ramonyx ships **primitives**, not a full auth product: safe cookies, HMAC-signed values, a signed
session cookie, and CSRF protection. Authentication flows (password/OAuth/etc.) stay in your app.

## Cookies

```ts
import { parseCookies, serializeCookie, expireCookie } from "@ramonyx/security";

const cookies = parseCookies(request.headers.get("cookie"));
const header = serializeCookie("theme", "dark", { path: "/", sameSite: "lax" });
```

Defaults for session cookies are safe: `path=/`, `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite=lax`.
`expireCookie(name)` produces `Max-Age=0`.

## Signed values

```ts
import { signValue, verifyValue } from "@ramonyx/security";

const signed = await signValue("user-42", env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!);
const value = await verifyValue(signed, env.get("SESSION_SECRET")!); // string | null
```

HMAC-SHA256 via Web Crypto with a constant-time comparison. The secret must come from env/bindings
(never hard-coded).

## Signed session cookie

```ts
const session = createSession({ secret: env.get("SESSION_SECRET")! });

// read (loader/middleware/action)
const data = await session.read(request);   // SessionData | null

// commit (action) — returns a Set-Cookie value
const cookie = await session.commit({ user: "rina" }, { maxAgeSeconds: 3600 });

// logout
const cleared = session.clear();
```

Options: `cookieName` (default `ramonyx_session`), `maxAgeSeconds` (default 7 days), and extra cookie
attributes (`domain`, `secure: false` for local HTTP).

```ts
export async function action({ request, env }) {
  const session = createSession({ secret: env.get("SESSION_SECRET")! });
  const user = await session.read(request);
  if (user === null) return { redirect: "/login" };
  return {
    message: `Hello ${String(user.user)}`,
    headers: { "set-cookie": await session.commit({ ...user, seen: true }) },
  };
}
```

Action results can return `headers`; `set-cookie` headers are applied to the re-render.

## CSRF

```ts
import { csrfProtection } from "@ramonyx/security";

export default [csrfProtection()];
```

Double-submit cookie + header:
- the middleware issues a signed token cookie when missing;
- state-changing requests (non-GET/HEAD) must echo the token in `x-csrf-token`;
- comparison is constant-time.

Client code can read the cookie (`httpOnly: false` for the CSRF cookie) and send the header. Forms
with JavaScript use the intercepted submit path; without JavaScript, use the standard form POST.

## Limitations (honest)

- **No auth package**: no user store, password hashing, OAuth providers, or authorization model.
  Build those in your app (or an ecosystem package).
- Hidden-field CSRF verification for non-JS form flows is **not implemented** (double-submit
  header is the supported path).
- `trustProxy` for rate limiting/client identity is opt-in; set it only behind a trusted proxy.
- The session cookie holds JSON; keep it small and non-secret (store large/secret data in a store and
  keep only an id in the cookie).

## docs/public/ssr-hydration.md

# SSR & Hydration

Ramonyx renders pages on the server, sends a hydration payload, and hydrates the same React tree in
the browser. Streaming is opt-in.

## What a request looks like

```
Request → middleware → route match → loader → render (React) → HTML document → Response
```

The document contains:

- the server-rendered markup inside `#ramonyx-root`,
- `<script id="ramonyx-payload">window.__RAMONYX__ = { path, params, data, action, locale }</script>`,
- the hashed client bundle (`/assets/client-<hash>.js`) that hydrates the tree and wires soft
  navigation, prefetch, and form interception.

Because the payload is embedded, there is no extra data request on hydration.

## Streaming (opt-in)

```ts
// ramonyx.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ app: { streaming: true } });
```

With `streaming: true`, the shell (head + layout) is sent immediately and the body is streamed with
`renderToReadableStream` (edge build of React). Errors after the first byte close the stream — the
status can no longer change. Error pages are always rendered synchronously.

## Layouts & error boundaries

- `layout.tsx` wraps pages in the folder and above; layouts receive `children`.
- `error.tsx` receives `{ error: { status, message, details? } }`. `details` (stack + source file)
  is only included outside production.
- Unknown paths fall through to a catch-all page (the template ships `[...slug]` with
  `metadata.status = 404`).

## Client behavior

| Feature | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Hydration | `hydrateRoot` on the existing markup; pages with islands hydrate only their marked boundaries |
| Deferred data | `defer()` + `<Suspense>` streams a server fallback, then the resolved boundary with a state script for hydration |
| Soft navigation | same-origin links fetch the next HTML, reconcile the head, swap the container, re-hydrate, `pushState` |
| Code splitting | client entry dynamically imports the active route/layout chunks; other routes load on navigation/prefetch |
| Prefetch | hover/focus/viewport prefetch HTML and warm the route chunk (LRU 8 entries, 30 s, max 2 concurrent) |
| Forms | submit intercepted when JS is available; `POST` + `303` PRG without JS |
| Scroll | `popstate` restores scroll; new navigations start at the top |

## Deferred loader data (streaming)

`defer()` starts non-critical work immediately and returns a thenable that can be read with
React's `use()` inside a `<Suspense>` boundary:

```tsx
import { defer, type Deferred } from "ramonyx";
import { Suspense, use } from "react";

export async function loader() {
  return {
    title: "Dashboard",
    stats: defer(() => loadStats()),
  };
}

function Stats({ value }: { value: Deferred<{ visits: number }> }) {
  const stats = use(value);
  return <p data-stats>{stats.visits} visits</p>;
}

export default function Dashboard({ data }: { data: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loader>> }) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{data.title}</h1>
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading stats…</p>}>
        <Stats value={data.stats} />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  );
}
```

- **Streaming is required** (`streaming: true`). The shell and a meaningful fallback are sent
  first; the resolved boundary follows and is revealed in the browser.
- **No-JS**: the fallback is the content users see. Make it useful (not an empty spinner); the
  final deferred value is progressively enhanced and is not available without JavaScript.
- The resolved values are serialized into a `<script type="application/json">` state tag after
  the mount container; the client reads it for hydration. Values must be JSON-serializable and
  must be rendered inside the boundary.
- **Soft navigation/actions** use a synchronous render; the client re-renders the deferred route
  from the state tag (avoiding React Suspense hydration mismatch). Prefetch, back/forward, and
  no-JS remain unchanged.
- A deferred rejection cannot change the response status after the first byte; React keeps the
  boundary fallback and switches it to client rendering, while `onError` logs the failure. Wrap
  recoverable failures with a React error boundary for a custom fallback.
- Deferred data is for non-critical UI. Keep critical content in the awaited loader result; do not
  combine deferred loader data with loader caching (`revalidate`).

## Code splitting & streaming boundaries

- The generated client entry uses dynamic imports per page/layout. The initial entry hydrates
  only the active route; other route chunks are loaded on navigation and warmed by prefetch.
- Streaming is active (`streaming: true`), but loaders resolve before render except data explicitly
  wrapped in `defer()`. Deferred boundaries are opt-in and retain a server-rendered fallback.
- Islands and deferred data are separate opt-ins. A page with islands hydrates only marked
  boundaries; a page with deferred data hydrates the route and client-renders it on soft
  navigation.

## Partial hydration islands (opt-in)

A page can mark interactive boundaries instead of hydrating the whole route. Register the client
component at module scope and render an `Island` with JSON-serializable props:

```tsx
import { defineIsland, Island } from "@ramonyx/react/islands";
import { useState } from "react";

function Counter({ start }: { start: number }) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(start);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount((value) => value + 1)}>Count: {count}</button>;
}

defineIsland("counter", Counter);

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <main>
      <p>Static server content.</p>
      <Island id="counter" props={{ start: 2 }} />
    </main>
  );
}
```

- The server renders the component inside a `data-ramonyx-island` wrapper. The client detects
  markers and calls `hydrateRoot` only on those wrappers; the rest of the route stays static.
- Detection is per page. **If a page contains any island, its whole route is island-hydrated** —
  every component that relies on React state, effects, or event props on that page or layout must
  be an `Island`. Document-level soft navigation and form interception still work for static
  markup.
- Island IDs are global and must be unique; props must be JSON-serializable (no functions,
  elements, `Date`/`Map`/`Set`, or circular references). Nested islands are not supported.
- Each island is an independent React root. React context from a static layout is not available;
  pass data through props or mount the provider inside the island. Shared state must live outside
  the island roots. React `useId` is supported because server and client use the same per-island
  identifier prefix.
- Soft navigation, prefetch, back/forward, and action re-renders hydrate the new page's islands;
  pages without islands keep the existing full-tree hydration. No-JS output is unchanged.
- Islands are a client-side boundary, not a server-component or data-loading feature.

## Soft navigation & head reconciliation

A soft navigation does not reload the document. Before the body is swapped, the client reconciles
the new document's head with the active one:

- `<title>` and `<html lang>`/`dir` are updated.
- `<meta>` and `<link>` tags are matched by their identity (`name`/`property`/`rel` + target);
  obsolete metadata and discovery links are removed.
- Inline `<style>` tags are staged with `media="not all"` and activated at the swap, so the old
  page keeps its styles until the new body is ready.
- External stylesheets are preloaded before the swap; the real `<link rel="stylesheet">` is then
  installed and the old styles/link are removed. The wait is capped at 2 seconds.
- New inline styles reuse the **current document's CSP nonce**, never the nonce embedded in the
  fetched document (the response's CSP header belongs to the active document).

The server document marks its generated style block with `data-ramonyx-style` so the client can
reconcile it without touching unrelated runtime nodes. Vite development styles are left alone.

### Boundaries

- `<script>` tags in the fetched head are not added or executed; the active client bundle remains
  responsible for navigation and hydration. Server-rendered payload data changes through
  `window.__RAMONYX__`, not through a new script.
- Nodes that are not part of the server head (for example Vite HMR styles) are preserved.
- Prefetch responses go through the same reconciliation path as normal navigation.
- If an external stylesheet fails to load, navigation continues after the timeout and falls back
  to the styles already in the document.

## Data loading & caching

Loaders run on the server on every request unless a page opts into caching:

```ts
export const revalidate = 60;                 // seconds (ISR-lite)
export const cacheTags = ["products"];        // for on-demand invalidation

export async function loader() {
  return { products: await db.products.list() };
}
```

- Responses that depend on a session (cookies) or query strings are **not** cached.
- Serve stale data while refreshing in the background (`stale-while-revalidate`).
- Invalidate on demand: `revalidate({ paths: ["/products"], tags: ["products"] })` from a loader,
  action (`context.revalidate`), or the cache instance.
- The default cache is in-memory per process; the store interface is pluggable for multi-instance
  deployments.

## Server actions

An `action` export turns a page into a mutation endpoint (POST to the same URL). It receives
`{ params, formData, request, env, log, locale, json(), revalidate() }` and can return
`{ message, errors, data, status, headers, redirect }`. A redirect is `303` (POST/Redirect/GET).

```ts
export async function action({ formData, revalidate }) {
  await db.notes.create({ text: String(formData.get("text") ?? "") });
  await revalidate({ tags: ["notes"] });
  return { message: "Saved" };
}
```

## Related primitives

- `AppHooks` (`onRequestStart/End`, `onLoaderEnd`, `onRenderEnd`, `onInvalidate`) for instrumentation.
- `traceId()`, `requestLogging()`, `createMetrics()` from `@ramonyx/server` for observability.
- Asset resolver + `Image` for hashed assets, responsive images, and anti-CLS dimensions.

## docs/public/testing.md

# Testing

Test the handler in-process (no ports, no runtime), then add browser tests for hydration and
progressive enhancement.

## In-process tests

`@ramonyx/testing` wraps a handler in an in-memory host:

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { createTestServerFromHandler } from "@ramonyx/testing";
import { createApp } from "../src/app.ts";

test("GET / renders SSR", async () => {
  const server = await createTestServerFromHandler(await createApp());
  try {
    const response = await server.fetch("/");
    assert.equal(response.status, 200);
    assert.match(await response.text(), /Hello/);
  } finally {
    await server.close();
  }
});
```

- `createTestServerFromHandler(handler)` — any `FetchHandler` (e.g. from `createApp`).
- `createTestServer({ routes, middleware })` — build a handler from route entries directly.
- `server.fetch(path | Request, init?)` resolves relative URLs against the in-memory origin.
- **Always `close()` in `finally`** — a leaked listener makes `node --test` hang.

## What to test

| Layer | Approach |
| --- | --- |
| Routing / params / methods | `server.fetch` — assert `200`, `404`, `405` + `Allow` |
| Validation | invalid query/params/body → `400` with `issues` |
| Loaders & actions | assert rendered HTML and the hydration payload |
| Cache/revalidate | call twice, assert loader counts and stale-while-revalidate behavior |
| Security | body limits (`413`), timeout (`503`), concurrency (`503` + `Retry-After`), CSRF |
| Browser | Playwright: hydration, soft navigation, forms with and without JS |

## Browser tests

The repo's playground runs Playwright against a production build (`pnpm build && pnpm test:e2e`).
For a new app:

```ts
// e2e/home.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";

test("hydrates and handles a form", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: /Click/ }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("button")).toHaveText(/1/);
});
```

Test **no-JS** by disabling JavaScript in the Playwright context: forms must still submit
(`POST` + `303` PRG).

## Commands

```bash
pnpm test          # node --test (packages, apps, tests, benchmarks)
pnpm test:e2e      # Playwright against a production build
pnpm test:docs     # this site's e2e (policy + a11y), if you vendor the docs app
```

## Tips

- Loader data must be JSON-serializable — assert the payload shape when in doubt.
- Use a fresh app/server per test for isolation; keep shared fixtures read-only.
- The dev scripts run app TypeScript/JSX through `@ramonyx/compiler/register` (no build step).

## docs/public/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Framework errors carry a stable code and a link to this page. Search the code below, or grab the
anchor from the error message.

## RMX-CONFIG-1 — invalid config

`ramonyx.config.ts` has a value with the wrong type.

| Field | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `app.strictValidation` | boolean |
| `app.streaming` | boolean |
| `server.port` | integer 0–65535 |
| `server.host` | non-empty string |

Fix the value; unknown keys are kept (config pass-through) and are not the cause.

## RMX-ROUTES-1 — can't read the routes directory

The compiler cannot read `src/routes` (missing directory or permissions). Create
`src/routes/page.tsx` or point the CLI at the right app with `--app`.

## RMX-ROUTES-2 — missing default export

A page/layout/error module has no `default` export. Every `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, and `error.tsx`
must export the component as default:

```tsx
export default function Page() { /* ... */ }
```

## RMX-ROUTES-3 — invalid middleware export

A `middleware.ts` must default-export an **array of functions**:

```ts
import type { Middleware } from "ramonyx";
export default [securityHeaders(), cspNonce()] satisfies Middleware[];
```

## RMX-ROUTES-4 — API route without an HTTP method export

An `api/**/*.ts` file exports none of `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS`. Export at
least one using `route({ handler })`.

## RMX-ROUTES-5 — invalid route definition

An exported method is not a route definition. Use the helper:

```ts
export const GET = route({
  handler: ({ json }) => json({ ok: true }),
});
```

## RMX-BUILD-1 — server import in a client module

A page/layout imports `node:*` directly. The client bundle cannot contain Node APIs. Move that code
into a `*.server.ts` module and call it from a loader/action/API route; the client bundle gets a
poison-pill stub instead of your server code.

## RMX-BUILD-2 — server code leaked into the client bundle

Same problem, but through a transitive import (or a Vite browser-external shim was found). Split the
server-only code behind `*.server.ts` and import it only from the server side.

## RMX-EDGE-1 — `node:*` in the edge artifact

The edge target rejects Node built-ins. `guardedFetch` lives in a Node-only subpath; import it from
`@ramonyx/security/ssrf` **only** in Node code, and keep edge code on `fetch`.

## Common non-coded issues

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `413` on POST | Body over 1 MiB. Raise `maxBodyBytes` in `createHandler` or stream/upload differently. |
| `503` after 10 s | Handler/loader/render timeout. Optimize, or raise `timeoutMs`. `request.signal` is aborted. |
| `503` + `Retry-After` under load | Concurrency limit (default 100) shedding load. Scale out or raise `maxConcurrent`. |
| Hydration mismatch / no interactivity | Client bundle not built (`ramonyx build` before `ramonyx start`) or an error page (error pages are not hydrated). |
| Assets 404 in production | Build first; assets are hashed into `dist/client` and served by `ramonyx start`. |
| `node_modules` TypeScript fails | Node does not type-strip `node_modules`; publish compiled JS for plugins/consumers. |
| Dev server panel missing | Open the URL printed by `ramonyx dev` (`/__ramonyx/devtools`); it is dev-only. |

## Getting more detail

- Development error pages include the stack and source file; production pages never do.
- The CLI `ramonyx doctor` prints config, route count, and build status.
- See [Testing](testing.md) for reproducing issues in-process.

## docs/public/typed-routes.md

# Typed Routes

`ramonyx build` and `ramonyx dev` generate `.ramonyx/routes.ts` from your page manifest. Use it to
make route paths and params type-safe at compile time.

## Generated module

```ts
// .ramonyx/routes.ts (generated — do not edit)
export type RouteParamsMap = {
  "/": undefined;
  "/users": undefined;
  "/users/[id]": { id: string };
  "/blog/[...slug]": { slug: string };
};

export function routeHref<P extends keyof RouteParamsMap>(
  path: P,
  ...args: RouteParamsMap[P] extends undefined ? [] : [params: RouteParamsMap[P]]
): string;
```

Import it with a **relative path** (there is no `#routes` alias yet):

```tsx
import { routeHref } from "../.ramonyx/routes.ts";

routeHref("/users");                  // "/users"
routeHref("/users/[id]", { id: "42" }); // "/users/42"
```

Wrong paths or missing params fail at type-check time. The generated file is refreshed on
`ramonyx dev` and `ramonyx build` — no manual step.

## `Link` component

`Link` from `@ramonyx/react/link` renders an `<a>` and uses the client navigation/prefetch path:

```tsx
import { Link } from "@ramonyx/react/link";

<Link href={routeHref("/users/[id]", { id: "42" })}>User 42</Link>;
```

`href` is a plain string; use `routeHref` to build it safely.

## Notes

- The module only exists after the first `build`/`dev` run.
- Import by relative path from your app code; a path alias is a candidate for a future release.
- The params map follows the file router: `[param]` → required single segment, `[...param]` → rest.
- Custom codegen? The manifest is the source; `generateRouteTypes(pages)` is exported from
  `@ramonyx/compiler` if you need it in another tool.

## Experimental runtime (Rust + V8)

Permission deny-all model, HTTP server with streaming/cancellation, worker and process isolation,
CPU/RSS quotas, plugin sandbox (Landlock), TLS `fetch`, CommonJS interop. Shipped as a separate
binary; **not part of the production promise** yet — see the repository for its assessments.
